page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 24 virtual CPUs mapped from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge in the average performance tier. The processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block bandwidth of 1282.13 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 48.03 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, it processes 1294.61 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, though performance drops to 34.44 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density offer predictable performance for general-purpose workloads without the overhead of GPU or bundled local storage. However, the lack of local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. This server is suited for workloads such as database operations, web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale text or image processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 24 vCPUs, 12 physical cores, and a 3.1 GHz clock speed. It is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core, but lacks local storage and GPU hardware. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate average performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 23015.19. The instance demonstrates strong utility for database operations, achieving 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving at 17.13 GB/sec. It is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, web serving, and software compilation where dedicated CPU resources are required without the need for local high-speed storage.
